cases.prompt: The validated onboarding story still works, but we want to redesign its information architecture and promises deliberately.
The project plan and epic map now exist. Have independent reviewers challenge the planning corpus before downstream specification begins.
This epic crosses two services, introduces a new shared contract, and adds a complex payment-provider integration. Design those seams before its technical plan.
The epic technical specification is complete. Turn it into dependency-ordered stories and close promise-to-story traceability before story work starts.
The epic document exists, but its boundaries and acceptance criteria can be interpreted several ways. Resolve those gaps before planning.
One epic needs technical principles that extend and partially override the project-wide constitution; the other epics do not.
This brownfield product has code and documentation but no epic structure. Discover coherent epic boundaries before specifying any epic.
The multi-screen epic feels like separate apps stitched together. Define entry states, handoffs, emotional progression, and the magic-moment placement before planning.
The UX-heavy epic is specified. Map user touchpoints, emotions, and end-to-end flow before wireframes and technical planning.
The epic scope is clear and its optional architecture work is done. Write the complete technical design and traceability before breaking it into stories.
Every story in the epic is validated. Synthesize their retrospectives into the epic learning artifact before closing the epic.
The project plan contains an epic placeholder. Turn it into the canonical epic vision and scope so the epic lifecycle can begin.
All stories are individually validated and the epic audit is complete. Prove the epic goals as a whole and declare its readiness.
The UX journey is complete. Create screen-by-screen states for the whole epic before its technical plan.
A shipped validation flow has a reproducible defect. Fix the bug, explain why the gates missed it, and add the systemic guardrail without redesigning the contract.
Before locking the accessibility requirement, check the current official standard and record the source that informs the decision.
Two independent epics can run concurrently. Define worktree isolation, seam contracts, and merge choreography before dispatching them.
This Platform project spans several systems and more than four epics. Design the project-wide architecture before creating the project plan.
I have a loose product idea but cannot yet state the concrete user problem or what should be built. Help crystallize it first.
The project vision exists, but the target users, goals, and scope boundaries are still underspecified. Fill those gaps before foundation work continues.
The Platform needs explicit project-wide coding principles, governance rules, and non-negotiable technical guardrails.
The Build project is clarified. Capture team capacity, stack boundaries, compliance, operational targets, and hard constraints before planning.
This UI Platform needs shared design tokens, a primitive registry, component standards, and visual governance before planning.
The healthcare product has regulated terminology, domain rules, and invariants complex enough to deserve a standalone model.
The product contract is locked. Define what counts as proof, what does not, the readiness gates, and adversarial probes before project planning.
Start this brownfield engagement by extracting goals, history, constraints, and team context from the existing documentation before scanning code or writing the vision.
The required product, evidence, context, and architecture foundations are complete. Create the PRD, epic structure, and E000 before any epic begins.
For this Build product, lock the differentiator, promises, banned language, and magic moments before project planning or epic work.
This started as a Sprint, but its scope and proof needs now require the full Build rigor and artifacts.
The product contract changed and the public root README now misstates the promise. Refresh the public profile from current truth.
Project validation passed. Synthesize all epic retrospectives and close this project phase with project-level learning.
The project plan exists. Sequence its epics, dependencies, resources, and milestones for a multi-team, multi-quarter Platform delivery.
The product problem is clear. Create the canonical project vision, users, value, boundaries, and success definition so the project can start.
Truth-affecting gates have landed on main. Regenerate the concise current-state artifact and next action from the canonical evidence.
Before planning this five-epic UI product, define the project-wide UX strategy, interaction principles, and experience direction.
Every epic is complete and validated. Prove the project-level outcomes and declare the highest readiness supported across the product.
Implementation just finished. Independently attack the acceptance criteria, negative paths, and evidence before allowing validation.
The v6-to-v7 migration ran, but the generated product and evidence contracts are still empty scaffolds and old readiness claims need honest backfill.
A Speck validation script is failing unexpectedly. Reproduce the failure, isolate the root cause, and diagnose the broken workflow.
We selected one provider after comparing alternatives. Record the locked choice, tradeoffs, rationale, date, and SHA at this phase boundary.
The methodology itself has a repeatable routing defect. Capture and deduplicate it as Speck feedback rather than product learning.
Run the quarterly scan of current autonomous-engineering methods and compare the frontier against Speck's methodology baseline.
The repository has a .speck/.v9-graph-needed marker. Establish and heal the witness graph before normal work proceeds.
Cold-start the target build and walk the job as a named persona, judging both whether it works and whether the experience is good.
A surprising integration gotcha was discovered mid-story and should become a reusable pattern now rather than wait for the formal retro.
Upgrade this existing repository to the current Speck version additively while preserving all prior artifacts.
Before granting UX-RC to this high-impact interface, challenge whether the contract's underlying design decision is worth building at all.
A new agent is taking over after three weeks away. Check current runtime and truth documents for drift before new feature work.
The repository has a .speck/.v8-reprove-needed marker. Re-evaluate v7-era green under the v8 evaluation standard.
Extract code-side facts for this brownfield epic so planning uses current implementation reality rather than assumptions.
We changed a methodology gate. Measure its fitness against seeded defects and compare the candidate score with the immutable baseline.
A non-trivial architecture choice is about to lock. Enumerate and compare at least three alternatives before recording the decision.
The story spec exists, but requirements, acceptance criteria, and scope are still ambiguous. Resolve those gaps before planning.
A legacy checkout feature already exists in code but has no Speck story artifacts. Reverse-engineer its story spec and code-side scan.
The story has reviewed spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md. Implement it completely, update tasks honestly, and stop before adversarial audit.
The clarified story specification is ready. Write its technical design, data contracts, and test strategy before creating implementation tasks.
Story validation passed. Capture what happened, mine the commits, and write the story learning artifact before epic synthesis.
The epic breakdown contains a draft story placeholder. Complete its user story, criteria, boundaries, and constraints before planning.
The story plan and optional UI specification are complete. Convert them into a dependency-ordered executable checklist before coding.
The story plan is done and the interface has multiple components, interaction states, animations, and complex layouts. Specify the exact UI before tasks.
The story implementation passed adversarial audit. Execute the prove gate, correct overclaims, and declare the highest readiness actually earned.
Review these user-facing components while they are being built and remove generic boilerplate so they express the project's visual personality.
During story validation, coordinate screenshots, accessibility evidence, and host-specific visual checks for the UI described in ui-spec.md.
